title: PostgreSQL18 Compose mounts the obsolete data directory
integration: present on reviewed main; no unmerged fix branch
summary: Both production and development Compose select postgres:18 but mount their named volume at /var/lib/postgresql/data. PostgreSQL18 defaults PGDATA to /var/lib/postgresql/18/docker and declares the volume at /var/lib/postgresql. The configured named volume therefore does not contain the actual database; current official image entrypoint also detects the obsolete mount and can refuse startup. This prevents reliable first installation and persistence across container recreation.
verification: Manual source trace; see issue and supplemental record for independent probes/scanner limits

title: Undiscoverable migrations leave notification columns absent and hide dormant view SQL
integration: present on reviewed main; no unmerged fix branch
summary: Four migration classes have neither MigrationAttribute nor DbContextAttribute in any partial file. EF migration discovery omits them. Two omitted classes duplicate changes made by later registered migrations, but AddNotificationRouteCooldownAndRecovery is the only actual migration adding CooldownMinutes and SendRecovery; later Designer models merely describe these fields. A database built by Migrate consequently lacks fields selected by the notification route entity and route operations fail. AddMonitorDataViews is also undiscoverable. These SQL views are not mandatory: the specification uses views for product time ranges, and current APIs query raw samples/rollups. Their absence is not a missing-feature finding. Its SQL additionally references unquoted mixed-case columns, which PostgreSQL folds to lowercase; simply adding attributes would fail. Adding attributes indiscriminately to the two duplicate migrations would create duplicate-column errors.
verification: Manual source trace; see issue and supplemental record for independent probes/scanner limits

title: Private IP HTTP bootstrap cannot establish required secure cookies
integration: present on reviewed main; no unmerged fix branch

The deployment initially serves the admin app over plain HTTP, while auth cookies always require Secure and antiforgery is also configured for secure transport. Browsers do not accept/send Secure cookies from plain HTTP private-IP origins; localhost has a special exception and does not prove LAN bootstrap works. Thus a user opening `http://192.168.x.x:<admin-port>` can submit credentials but cannot retain the authenticated wizard session. Final HTTPS is configured inside that wizard, creating an additional first-install transport dependency.

title: Fresh setup requires an unlocked vault before the wizard creates it
integration: present on reviewed main; no unmerged fix branch

The implementation avoids storing EAB material in plaintext and `CertificateSetupService.SaveAsync` returns failure unless `VaultSessionState.IsUnlocked`. On a fresh installation, no vault can be unlocked at the certificate step because the wizard has not yet reached the step that creates the recovery-key wrap and registers the passkey. The certificate step UI only advances when that save succeeds, and it has no defer/skip action. A user following the provided wizard cannot reach vault setup through the normal UI.

title: Firewall NAT chains are created in the filter table

If the host already has nat chains from an earlier deployment, the script does not flush those nat chains and appends new rules instead, so stale forwarding can survive. Every secret DEK also has an admin-root wrap, including generic session-only secrets with IsServiceSyncEligible=false. In addition InitializePurposeKey has no production caller; GetPurposeWrapKeyOrThrow falls back to the same global wrap key for every purpose. Authenticators that report a zero sign counter do not provide a counter-based replay signal, so replay may create additional admin sessions or repeat reauthentication.

summary: An authenticated session can register another passkey without recent passkey reauthentication. The registration endpoints are mutating `/api/auth/passkeys/register/*` routes, but `AdminApiAuthMiddleware` does not classify registration as a `security.manage` operation or as requiring recent reauthentication. `afterSetup=true` explicitly enables registration after setup, so the server accepts this credential-enrollment path even though the current UI only exposes it during setup. title: Trailing slash on secret reveal bypasses reauth and secret scope

summary: The route `/api/vault/secrets/{id}/reveal` also matches with a trailing slash, while the middleware recognizes secret reveal using the raw path's `EndsWith("/reveal")`. For `/reveal/`, both special checks fail. Because it is a GET, RequiredScope falls through to `admin.read` and RequiresReauthentication returns false. The endpoint handler then decrypts and returns a secret if that session's vault is unlocked. Thus a stale reauth session can reveal a secret, and a session lacking secrets.manage is not rejected by that scope guard. This does not bypass ordinary login, IP binding or the need for an unlocked session vault.

title: Client supplied geo headers can bypass country region and ASN rules
integration: present on reviewed main; no unmerged fix branch
summary: EdgeAuthEndpoints trusts X-Geo-Country/Region/Asn whenever the immediate peer is a trusted proxy. The generated Traefik forwardAuth configuration has no authRequestHeaders allowlist or middleware stripping/replacing those client headers. Traefik forwards all request headers by default. An external client can therefore send all three geo headers through the legitimate trusted proxy, suppress the local GeoIP lookup, and choose the metadata evaluated by geo rules. Trusting the transport peer does not establish the provenance of these arbitrary headers. This applies to the generated configuration unless another independently configured upstream sanitizes them.

The router can therefore send a request to one resource while Hashi evaluates another resource's rules/manual scope/provider/CAP identity. Strict mode enforces SSO generically but does not repair wrong resource-specific rules or scopes. Database enumeration order is not a deterministic routing policy.

During the interval before chmod, local users may also read it. This is a DNS provider credential exposure on the managed host.

title: Firewall SSH-risk check trusts an unvalidated forwarded header
integration: present on reviewed main; no unmerged fix branch
summary: Firewall planning and apply logic take the first `X-Forwarded-For` value directly from the request and use it as the operator's IP. They do not use `ForwardedClientContextResolver`, which only honors forwarding headers when the immediate peer is a configured trusted proxy. A direct caller can therefore spoof an address that is allowed by the planned firewall. The apply guard then skips the “would block your current connection” warning and does not require `AcknowledgeSshBlockRisk`, even if the real caller address would be blocked. The global sync plan and apply paths repeat this raw-header parsing, so both preview and enforcement can use a spoofed address.
verification: Manual source trace; see issue and supplemental record for independent probes/scanner limits

Neither output references an environment file or otherwise injects the script's configured variables. title: DNS subnet matcher accepts out-of-range CIDR prefixes
integration: present on reviewed main; no unmerged fix branch
summary: `DnsRecordGenerator.IpMatchesSubnet` parses the prefix as an integer but never checks that it lies between zero and the address width (32 for IPv4, 128 for IPv6). With matching address families, a negative prefix can reach the comparison loop and match arbitrary addresses; a prefix larger than the address width can index beyond the address byte array. The helper is used to associate resource/agent addresses with firewall hosts from persisted `ManagedSubnets` and `NetBirdRoutedCidrs`, so malformed stored CIDR metadata can select the wrong host or throw while constructing DNS desired state.

title: Manual DNS records are not validated by type or DNS constraints

summary: `DnsRecordService.ValidateAsync` checks that the zone exists, the type is one of five supported values, the name and value are nonempty, TTL is positive, and exact local duplicates are absent. It does not validate record values by type, ensure the owner name is valid/in-scope for the selected zone, or enforce DNS constraints such as a CNAME not coexisting with other data at the same owner name. Invalid values and conflicting records are therefore persisted as desired state and fail later at provider sync, or can generate an invalid zone state.

title: DNS CRUD and planner collapse multi-value RRsets
integration: present on reviewed main; no unmerged fix branch
summary: The DNS model represents provider records individually, but `DnsPlanner` treats only MX and TXT as multi-value types. For A, AAAA, and NS records it indexes only one row per name/type and keys desired values without the value. `DnsRecordService.ValidateAsync` likewise prevents a second A/AAAA/NS value at the same owner name. Providers can hold multiple values in those RRsets, so the UI cannot represent them and planner indexing silently drops all but one current/desired value. The current Hetzner replacement API also operates on RRsets, which makes the one-record-per-owner/type assumption especially incompatible.
verification: Manual source trace; see issue and supplemental record for independent probes/scanner limits

It also accepts any hostname that ends in `.{AdminDomain}`, rather than only the configured admin domain. If a proxy passes client-supplied forwarding headers through, or the setup request is made through an arbitrary subdomain, the endpoint can mark HTTPS verification complete without verifying HTTPS on the exact configured admin hostname.

title: Access log ingestion rereads whole files and misses some rotations

summary: On every one-minute run, `AccessLogIngestWorker` reads the complete configured remote access log over SFTP into memory, then slices the byte array at the saved offset. If rotation replaces the file with a new file whose length is greater than or equal to the previous offset, the worker resumes at that offset and permanently skips the new file's leading entries.
verification: Manual source trace; see issue and supplemental record for independent probes/scanner limits

title: Subsystem apply endpoints bypass the shared sync lock
integration: present on reviewed main; no unmerged fix branch
summary: Global apply and reconcile acquire a process-level `ApplyLock` plus a PostgreSQL advisory lock. The separate DNS, Traefik, and firewall apply endpoints call their provider services directly, and those services do not acquire either shared lock. A direct subsystem apply can therefore overlap a global apply or background reconcile for the same connection/host. The calls can both recheck the same prior state, then interleave remote writes, service reloads, and last-applied state updates; a returned success or stored hash may describe only one operation's view of the resulting remote configuration.

YAML validation can catch malformed YAML but does not prevent a syntactically valid Traefik rule from being broadened by an embedded backtick/operator. Ordinary administrator input can therefore create a broken or wider-than-intended route and/or alter the generated service URL.

title: Monitor latency summary reports rollup averages as sample min/max/average
integration: present on reviewed main; no unmerged fix branch
summary: The status page calculates its min, max, and average from each rollup's `AverageLatencyMs`. Those values are averages for time buckets, not the individual probe latencies.
